recall_prompt: Say how you would prove this — name each move in order.

steps.label: Write as fractions and combine
steps.margin_note: First mark. cosec and sec are reciprocals, so write them out and combine over one denominator.

recall.must_convey: That cosec and sec are written as reciprocals and the two terms combined over sin20° cos20°.
accept: write cosec as one over sin and sec as one over cos then combine over a common denominator
convert the reciprocals and put over one denominator
express both as fractions and combine
cosec sec ni fractions ga rasi common denominator teeskovali
combine into a single fraction

steps.why: cosec and sec are just 1/sin and 1/cos. Writing them out is always the first move when they appear in an identity.

steps.label: Take 2 out to make known angles
steps.margin_note: Second mark. This time √3/2 and 1/2 land as sin 60° and cos 60° — the other way round from the twin.

recall.must_convey: That 2 is factored out, making the coefficients √3/2 and 1/2, recognised as sin60° and cos60°.
accept: take two out so root three by two is sin sixty and half is cos sixty
factor the two and the coefficients become sixty degree values
root three over two is sin sixty this time
two common teeste sin sixty cos sixty vasthai
recognise the values as sixty degrees

steps.why: The √3 sits on the cosine here rather than the sine, which is why the angle comes out as 60° instead of 30°.

steps.label: Apply sin(A−B)
steps.margin_note: Third mark. The numerator collapses to 2 sin 40°.

recall.must_convey: That sinA cosB − cosA sinB = sin(A−B) is applied, giving 2 sin40°.
accept: apply the sin A minus B formula to get two sin forty
the numerator becomes two sin forty degrees
use the compound angle formula
sin A minus B formula tho two sin forty vasthundi
the top collapses to two sin forty

steps.why: Sixty minus twenty is forty, and forty is twice twenty — which is exactly what makes the denominator cancel next.

steps.label: Expand sin40° and cancel
steps.margin_note: Last mark. sin40° = 2 sin20° cos20°, the denominator exactly — so it cancels and leaves 4.

recall.must_convey: That sin40° = 2 sin20° cos20° cancels the denominator, leaving 4.
accept: sin forty is two sin twenty cos twenty which cancels leaving four
expand and everything cancels to four
the denominator cancels and the answer is four
sin forty ni expand cheste anni cancel ayi four vasthundi
only four is left after cancelling

steps.why: Both twins land on 4 for the same reason: the angle in the numerator is always double the one in the denominator.
